trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data, of a merchant's gateway account, or of a company console account
deadline: Immediately and no later than 24 hours after suspicion
notify: Processor partner's and sponsor bank's recorded incident contacts (recorded by 2026-09-15, POAM-008)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised, Visa Supplemental Requirements v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa payment account data or to a payment system that stores, processes, or transmits it
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations; acquirers and their processors report through Visa's case tool, so the company reports through the processor partner and sponsor bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Section A applies to any entity with access to a payments environment, including agents and service providers

obligation: Visa notice to other relevant parties
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise event
deadline: Immediately
notify: Acquiring bank (the sponsor bank, through the processor partner) and other relevant parties; Visa also strongly recommends law enforcement and legal counsel
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

trigger: Notice given to Visa under A.1
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
notify: Visa and the acquiring bank (incident report form, Attachment A), with PCI DSS documentation when available or requested
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - prepared with the processor partner

trigger: Discovery of compromised account data; Visa's request; or the window of exposure is determined
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of the trigger
notify: Visa, through the acquirer or processor's upload to Visa's case tools
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the processor partner pulls the card list from gateway records; the company supplies the window of exposure

obligation: PCI forensic investigation (if Visa requires one)
trigger: Formal notice from Visa that a PCI Forensic Investigator (PFI) is required
deadline: Contract with a PFI within 5 business days; preliminary report within 5 business days of retaining the PFI; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation
notify: Visa and the acquiring bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Visa requires it; the PFI must not be affiliated with the company or have provided it other services such as security assessments (WTDIC A.5.3)

citation: Each brand's rules, through the sponsor bank
trigger: Suspected compromise involving that brand's cards
deadline: Per each brand's rules (timing not verified here; the sponsor bank confirms)
notify: Brand, through the sponsor bank
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - handled through the processor partner and sponsor bank

trigger: Acquisition of unencrypted customer information without the individual's authorization (unauthorized access presumed to be acquisition absent reliable evidence otherwise) involving the information of at least 500 consumers
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 days after discovery (first day known to any employee, officer, or agent other than the person committing the breach)
notify: Federal Trade Commission, through the electronic form on ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the 314.6 exception does not cover paragraph (j). Counsel decides whether card data captured on the processor partner's page is customer information handled on the company's behalf; plan as if it is

trigger: A law enforcement official provides a written determination that public notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Initial delay of up to 30 days after notice to the FTC; up to 60 more days on written request; further delay only if FTC staff agrees
notify: Include in the FTC notice; FTC contacts the official
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Third-party agent notice to merchants (Florida worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of a system maintained by the company for merchants (covered entities) involving personal information of Florida residents (name plus card number with any required security code)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: Each affected merchant, with all information it needs for its own notices; the company may send notices for the merchant (501.171(6)(b))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where counsel finds the company acted as the merchants' third-party agent; otherwise the processor partner, which hosts the page, carries this duty. Plan to the 10-day clock either way

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (covered entity duty)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents where the company is the covered entity (merchant owner data), or when sending notices for a merchant
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (15 more days with good cause given in writing to the department)
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes when the company owns the data or sends notices for a merchant

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred (the 15-day extension applies only to individual notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents and the company is the covered entity (otherwise the merchant's duty)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents; definitions and third-party agent rules vary
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Merchants (as data owners); residents; state attorneys general or regulators where required
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 8% of merchants are outside Florida, and online shoppers can live anywhere; apply the law of each state where affected residents live

obligation: Inbound third-party agent notice to the company (Florida worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained for the company by a vendor (CRM vendor, phone vendor, MSP, web hosting) involving personal information
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after the vendor's determination
notify: The company (Operations Manager)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to the MSP contract and confirm in vendor terms

trigger: Suspected security incident, account takeover, or extortion demand
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if an extortion demand is made

citation: None (voluntary); Visa WTDIC v10.0 A.3 recommends it
trigger: Criminal compromise of payment data or refund fraud
deadline: As soon as practicable; coordinate with counsel
notify: U.S. Secret Service field office (Visa names its Electronic Crimes Task Forces) or FBI through IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

trigger: Computer-security incident that materially disrupts or degrades covered services to a banking organization customer for four or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible after the determination
notify: Bank-designated point of contact, or the bank's CEO and CIO
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company performs no covered services for the sponsor bank (P03 section 1.3). The ISO agreement's 24-hour notice applies instead

obligation: Banking organization notification incident (sponsor bank's own duty)
trigger: Notification incident at a banking organization
deadline: No later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident occurred
notify: OCC supervisory office (by the bank)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the sponsor bank's duty. The company's 24-hour contract notice gives the bank what it needs to decide

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours (ransom payment). Not yet effective
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final

trigger: SCI event at an SCI entity
deadline: Immediately; written notice within 24 hours
notify: SEC
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an SCI entity

trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: No later than 72 hours
notify: NCUA
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a credit union and serves none

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article from Kaspersky Lab
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
